correctness.rationale: A reconstructed proof establishes continuity of unique support minimizers, a strictly positive compact fixed-separation support modulus, the standard smoothness descent bound, convergence to the compact minimizer set, and an exhaustive two-branch inverse-gap increment argument. For arbitrary fixed K choose small epsilon; small displacements force increment >K and all large displacements force increment >K as optimizer distance vanishes. Cesaro averaging gives tF_t->0. The explicit superflat body has h>0 off the origin, strict convexity through zero, a strictly concave top, and support ratio o(|x|^q) for all finite q. No numerical sampling is relied on.

originality.rationale: The 2026 motivating theorem requires fixed-power LDS, while its own superflat example defeats every exponent. The 2021 antecedent assumes power-type curvature in its convergence theorems. Dunn (1979, 1980) has important earlier non-power exposure results that cover a nonzero-gradient constrained-minimizer subclass, but its abstract-stated optimum-gradient exposure modulus vanishes when the gradient at the optimum is zero. The present all-objectives theorem includes that excluded case. Since Dunn full texts are inaccessible, further coverage by them is an explicit substantial originality risk.
residual_risks: Possible uncatalogued earlier qualitative support-modulus Frank–Wolfe asymptotic result; negative search evidence cannot exclude it.
The novelty comparison to older broad methods is limited to the specifically inspected published statements and accessible full texts.
No quantitative uniform convergence exponent or empirical speedup is implied by strict convexity alone.

The two relevant historical Dunn manuscripts were not available for full-text examination. Their primary abstracts establish meaningful partial overlap, and their uninspected complete texts could contain broader coverage.

value.rationale: Answers the meaningful gap exposed in the motivating 2026 paper: its superflat strictly convex counterexample defeats every power-type LDS theorem, while our power-free geometric theorem nevertheless guarantees per-instance improvement over the universal O(1/t) baseline for every smooth convex objective. It identifies strict support exposure, not curvature exponent or objective growth, as a sufficient qualitative mechanism, valid with vanishing gradient and arbitrary minimizer multiplicity. The implication is mathematical rather than a routine renaming of LDS parameters: no fixed polynomial parameter exists for the example.
